cues: From chlorobenzene, by the Dow process: sodium hydroxide at three hundred degrees and a hundred and fifty atmospheres, since chlorobenzene is so unreactive.
From benzene diazonium chloride, simply by warming its acidic solution above five degrees, so nitrogen bubbles off: the mild laboratory method.
And from benzene sulphonic acid, by fusing its sodium salt with solid sodium hydroxide.
text: Three ways to make phenol. From chlorobenzene, by the Dow process: sodium hydroxide at three hundred degrees and a hundred and fifty atmospheres, since chlorobenzene is so unreactive. From benzene diazonium chloride, simply by warming its acidic solution above five degrees, so nitrogen bubbles off: the mild laboratory method. And from benzene sulphonic acid, by fusing its sodium salt with solid sodium hydroxide.
